GLOSSARY.TITLE: Glossary
GLOSSARY.SUBTITLE: What each number means and how it is calculated

XIRR.TITLE: Total XIRR
XIRR.DESC: The true yearly return of the investment. It accounts for both the amount and the date of every deposit and withdrawal: money deposited a month ago should not "earn" like money that has been invested for five years. This is the right number for comparing investments.
XIRR.FORMULA:
Find r such that:
Σ flow ÷ (1 + r) ^ (days since start ÷ 365) = 0
Deposit = negative flow, withdrawal and current value = positive flow
XIRR.EXAMPLE: You deposited 10,000 ₪ a year ago and 10,000 ₪ half a year ago, and the value today is 21,500 ₪. Profit is 1,500 ₪, but half the money was invested for only half a year, so XIRR ≈ 10%, not 7.5%.

XIRR_YEARLY.TITLE: XIRR by year
XIRR_YEARLY.DESC: The same calculation as total XIRR, for one calendar year. The previous year-end value counts as if deposited at the start of the year, and only that year's deposits are counted. A first year with a single snapshot has no period to measure and shows "-". A year that has not ended yet is shown as a yearly rate.
XIRR_YEARLY.FORMULA:
Flows: −previous year-end value, −deposits of the year, +withdrawals of the year, +year-end value
then solve as in XIRR
XIRR_YEARLY.EXAMPLE: Value at end of 2024: 40,000 ₪, no deposits in 2025, value at end of 2025: 44,000 ₪. XIRR for 2025 = 10% and yearly profit = 4,000 ₪.

CAGR.TITLE: CAGR
CAGR.DESC: Average yearly growth of the value, compounded, from the first snapshot to the last. It only looks at the value and knows nothing about deposits, so it fits only an investment you do not deposit into. With regular deposits it is heavily inflated; use XIRR instead.
CAGR.EXAMPLE: 100,000 ₪ that grew to 121,000 ₪ in two years with no deposits: (1.21)^(1/2) − 1 = 10% a year.

TOTAL_PROFIT.TITLE: Total profit
TOTAL_PROFIT.DESC: How much the investment earned in shekels beyond the money you put in.
TOTAL_PROFIT.FORMULA: Total profit = current value − total deposits + total withdrawals
TOTAL_PROFIT.EXAMPLE: You deposited 35,000 ₪, withdrew nothing, and the value today is 51,000 ₪: total profit 16,000 ₪.

PERIOD_DEPOSITS.TITLE: Deposits in period
PERIOD_DEPOSITS.DESC: The money you put in (minus what you withdrew) between the previous snapshot and this one. This is the part of the value change that is not profit.
PERIOD_DEPOSITS.FORMULA:
Deposits in period = Σ deposits − Σ withdrawals
(after the previous snapshot, up to and including this one)
PERIOD_DEPOSITS.EXAMPLE: 11 deposits of 1,024 ₪ and one of 1,424 ₪ during the year: 12,688 ₪.

PERIOD_PROFIT.TITLE: Profit in period
PERIOD_PROFIT.DESC: How much the portfolio itself gained or lost between two snapshots, after removing deposits.
PERIOD_PROFIT.FORMULA: Profit in period = current value − previous value − deposits in period

PERIOD_RETURN.TITLE: Return in period (Modified Dietz)
PERIOD_RETURN.DESC: The profit in the period as a percentage of the money actually invested. Each deposit counts by the part of the period it was invested, so a mid-period deposit counts as half. The percentage is for the period itself, not yearly, so it also works for snapshots close together.
PERIOD_RETURN.FORMULA:
Return = profit ÷ (previous value + Σ deposit × weight)
weight = days from deposit to end of period ÷ days in period
PERIOD_RETURN.EXAMPLE: Previous value 1,000 ₪, a 1,000 ₪ deposit mid-period, current value 2,100 ₪. Profit 100 ₪, invested 1,000 + 1,000 × 0.5 = 1,500 ₪, return 6.7%.

VALUE_CHANGE.TITLE: Change in value
VALUE_CHANGE.DESC: The raw change in value between two snapshots. It includes deposits, so it is not a return: when the previous value is small and you deposited a lot, it can reach thousands of percent. Shown when hovering the value in the table.
VALUE_CHANGE.FORMULA: Change in value = (current value − previous value) ÷ previous value
VALUE_CHANGE.EXAMPLE: From 233 ₪ to 11,143 ₪: +4,682%, even though the portfolio actually lost 1,778 ₪.

SNAPSHOT.TITLE: Value snapshot
SNAPSHOT.DESC: The value of the portfolio on a given date, as shown in the provider's statement. Every calculation relies on snapshots, so one wrong snapshot distorts two periods: the one ending at it (profit too low or too high) and the one starting at it (the opposite way).
SNAPSHOT.FORMULA:
Snapshot = (date, portfolio value on that date)
Deposits are not entered here; they go in "Transactions"
SNAPSHOT.EXAMPLE: If a year-end snapshot holds the yearly deposit total by mistake instead of the value, that year looks like a big loss and the next year like a big gain.
